tb21_profile.skill: Implement a published Monte Carlo sampling algorithm (envelope/squeeze rejection sampling on a log-concave density) correctly, validate its own stochastic output against known distributions, and validate user inputs
tb21_profile.domain: R language, numerical statistics / Monte Carlo sampling, density functions and goodness-of-fit
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec (a paper) plus author your own PASS/FAIL test harness for stochastic output

TMax-15K.reason: Rejection sampling from an explicit PDF, derive the analytical CDF yourself, then verify samples by KS distance across sample sizes.
Monte Carlo rejection sampling from an unnormalized density plus a convergence harness comparing generated samples to a reference distribution.
Actual R scripting: ks.test against pgamma, ECDF vs fitted analytical CDF. Only corpus item exercising R statistical idioms.
Write a sampler from scratch and validate its stochastic output against the exact conjugate posterior mean/variance, the same validation problem.
Sample an unnormalized density f(x) from scratch and check moments against numerically integrated ground truth; same correctness argument.
Rejection sampling with a uniform proposal bounding box to hit a target normal density, graded by KS D-statistic; service plumbing is noise.
MCMC sampling of a known posterior with analytical validation of the samples; teaches how to prove a stochastic generator is correct.
Builds the convergence test for a Monte Carlo sampler against the exact exponential CDF, which is the grading half of the TB2.1 task.
Rejection-sampling Monte Carlo estimate of the normalizing constant of an unnormalized PDF, cross-checked against trapezoidal integration.
Complete an incomplete Metropolis-Hastings sampler module against a physical model; sampler implementation in a modular codebase.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Implement sqrt from scratch, validate numerically to a tolerance against a reference, and correct the reference when it disagrees.
Implement to a discovered spec and add a --self-test mode that runs internal checks and reports pass/fail, mirroring the required test() function.
Same family: implement full CLI from spec with self-test evidence and error-case handling for invalid invocations.
Implement a mathematical protocol (Diffie-Hellman) from the signatures and docstrings already present, i.e. implement-from-spec of an algorithm.
Fix a numerical function's edge case and add the missing test for it, then produce a validation report; weak input-validation overlap only.
Implement a classical numeric algorithm (Euclid) faithfully from its mathematical definition; algorithm fidelity but trivial depth.
Author a test project from scratch and report example/failure counts; the testing-harness half of TB2.1 with no statistics.
Initialize a test suite validating a function's expected behaviour; same test-authoring genre, unrelated subject matter.
Simulate random lottery outcomes with numeric input handling; touches randomness and input validation but no distributional correctness.
Compute GCDs and summary statistics over discovered input; only shares file-producing chore shape, no algorithmic or statistical demand.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Numerical-accuracy demonstration measured as mean absolute error against a known exact solution; same 'prove the numerics are right' work.
Property-based testing over randomly generated floats: how to assert a property on stochastic output, which TB2.1's test() must do.
Numerical optimization on a real problem in a scientific language ecosystem; adjacent numerical-methods capability, no sampling.
Implement a combinatorial algorithm from spec with CLI flags and per-case output files; same implement-and-emit shape, no statistics.
Run a statistical anomaly-detection estimator with specified parameters on a dataset; same broad area, no algorithm implementation.
Add seeding to an RNG-driven script so repeated runs reproduce; reproducibility of stochastic output is a sub-skill TB2.1 needs.
Implement a modular two-module system to a specified class/method interface; matches the modularity-and-consistent-design requirement only.
Author a working test suite from scratch including fixtures and discovery; the testing-infrastructure half, nothing statistical.
Write scientific-language code that must print interpretable, checkable demonstrations of each numeric claim to a log.
Implement a mathematical predicate from spec and produce exact output; implement-from-spec genre, unrelated stack and no stochasticity.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: Patsy implements R's formula language; the bug is failure to reject an invalid model specification, i.e. statistical-API input validation.
Reasoning about whether a generator's output is actually uniformly random and fixing its entropy source; random-number quality reasoning.
Restore a ValueError on negative input instead of silently returning garbage; exactly the 'reject negative sample counts' validation duty.
Algorithm returns wrong values and fails a mathematical symmetry test; debugging a numeric algorithm against a provable property.
Running mean/variance statistics fail to update correctly; estimating distribution parameters from streamed samples and checking them.
Missing 2D residual case in least-squares; numerical linear algebra correctness against a reference implementation's semantics.
Similarity algorithm produces incorrect values for custom parameter matrices; tracing a numeric algorithm back to its definition.
Restore removed methods of a distance algorithm class so the modular API works again; modular-algorithm-implementation overlap only.
Incorrect piecewise loss math and counting; fixing a small numerical formula against its published definition.
Statistical classifier gives wrong detections; debugging a probabilistic scoring routine, but no sampling or test authoring.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Binomial/beta-binomial logpmf returns NaN at k=n=0; reasoning about density-function edge cases and validating against scipy truth.
Bernoulli sampler is wrong for small p because float32 uniforms lack resolution; exactly the numerical-soundness reasoning a sampler needs.
MCMC sampling loses determinism under generator seeding; same territory of making stochastic sampler output reproducible and testable.
MCMC returns no samples for a degenerate model and the summary crashes; sampler-API edge-case handling in a probabilistic library.
Implementation deviates from the published paper's description and must be reconciled with it, the same fidelity-to-a-paper demand.
Special functions silently underflow to zero at large arguments; log-domain/overflow care is what keeps an ARS envelope numerically sane.
Replace rejection sampling of constrained values with construction that satisfies the predicate; direct reasoning about rejection efficiency.
Implement a sampling-measurement method to a written spec with worked examples and add unit tests for it; implement-plus-test genre.
Polylog gives garbage at infinite arguments; handling domain boundaries of a mathematical function before evaluating it.
Residual variance from a simulated forecast does not match the model's analytic expectation; reconciling simulation output with theory.

final_top10.reason: Rejection sampling from a given PDF, derive the analytical CDF, verify by KS distance and convergence; the closest match in the pool.
Rejection sampling an unnormalized density plus a convergence harness against a reference sample; both halves of TB2.1.
Real R statistical scripting with ks.test and ECDF-vs-analytical-CDF validation; the only R plus goodness-of-fit task found.
Hand-written sampler checked against the exact conjugate posterior; teaches how to test a stochastic routine against known truth.
Sampling an unnormalized f(x) and validating moments against numerically integrated ground truth in one self-contained program.
Rejection sampling with a bounding-box proposal to match a target density, graded by KS D-statistic threshold.
Density-function edge cases returning NaN; the same careful reasoning about log-densities at domain boundaries ARS requires.
Sampler wrong for small probabilities due to uniform-resolution limits; numerical soundness of a random sampler.
Generate samples from a known posterior and validate them analytically; same gold-standard-generator-plus-proof structure.
Reconcile an implementation with the published paper's description of the algorithm, exactly TB2.1's Gilks-and-Wild fidelity problem.

notes: R is essentially absent from all five corpora (one Red-language file, a handful of TMax tasks with auxiliary .R scripts), so the domain axis is carried by numerical-statistics content rather than by language. TMax-15K is by far the strongest pool: it has genuine rejection-sampling and sampler-validation tasks. Recursive-Task-Synthesis and TerminalWorld are weak; their retrieval shortlists were dominated by number-guessing-game and PASS/FAIL-report boilerplate, which I discarded, and my own searches confirmed neither corpus contains Monte Carlo or density-estimation work. Their entries are ranked on the two residual sub-skills (implement-from-spec, author your own test harness) and scored low accordingly. SWE-Smith has no statistics library of substance; patsy (R formula language) and pydicom's RNG-quality issue are the only defensible domain hits.
